summary: Soshuku Shibatani is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and earned an MA and PhD at Koyasan University. He held researcher posts at Koyasan University, lectured at Sonoda Women's University, and served at Junrei Henro Kenkyukai.

Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served as a professor, dean, and president at Komazawa University and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku (1860–1919) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University and under several masters, including Kōsen Imakita. He was Zen master at Engaku-ji, served at Nagata Zendo, and was president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma is a religious studies and Indology scholar. After studying at the University of Delhi and completing a PhD at Rice University, she taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, and Harvard, and became an instructional professor at the University of Houston.

Sravani Kanamarlapudi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied under Richard G. Salomon, attended the University of Washington, and pursued PhD studies at the University of Texas at Austin.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and earned a PhD at the University of Marburg, later serving as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.
Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He pursued his education at Sanskrit College and University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Dhaka.

Srikanth Kaul was an Indology and history scholar. In 1967, he is attested as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir and as holding a post at Government Degree College, Sopore.

Srinivas H. Ritti (1928–2021) was an Indology and history scholar. He served as an epigraphical assistant with the Archaeological Survey of India and Government Epigraphist for India, and later as Professor of Ancient Indian History and Epigraphy at Karnatak University.
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Sriram Krishnan is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Government College University, Lahore, worked as a vakil at Allahabad High Court, became a fellow at the University of Allahabad, and founded the Panini Office in 1891.

Stacey Van Vleet is a Tibetology, sinology, and history scholar. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed a PhD and held an academic post at Columbia University.

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, linguistics, and other fields. He was employed by the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1824 and founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, serving as its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He held chairs at the Collège de France and INALCO, and served at the Institut de France and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University. He held positions at psychiatric institutions in Czechoslovakia, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences and Warsaw Scientific Society.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in history, art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.
Stanley Cecil Sutton (1907–1993) was an Indology and history scholar who served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme, and served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale from circa 1974 to 2012.
